points.description: A static local array is initialised only once (the first time the function is called), whereas a non-static array is initialised every time the function is called. Accept any wording that conveys that static initialisation happens once and persists across calls, while a normal array is set up afresh each call.
points.partial_credit: Half marks (2-3) for a related statement that gets one half: e.g. says static arrays keep their value between calls, or that static arrays are created once, without saying how a normal array differs.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that a static array is initialised only once (on the first call) and not on each call, in any wording, including a brief comparison with ordinary arrays being re-initialised each call. Give 2 to 4 if the student captures only half of the fact, such as saying static arrays persist between calls or are created once, without the contrast. Give 0 to 2 for remarks about scope, memory location or speed that do not state the one-time initialisation. Extra correct detail costs nothing.
